messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT — High 5xx rate from eu-west-1 observed on the API gateway and customer-facing routes. Pager escalated to SRE primary. Monitoring shows ~30% of requests failing from EU egress IPs :rotating_light:
alice.sre: on it. I'm seeing NXDOMAINs and SERVFAILs for some subdomains when queried via Cloudflare resolvers. Route53 appears to have correct records for those names.
frank.oncall: paging ben and eve, net and infra. can we determine if this is resolver-side or authoritative?
ben.net: reproducing locally — when hitting Cloudflare's public resolvers (1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1) we get intermittent NXDOMAIN for api.eu.example.com, but dig directly against route53 nameservers returns correct A records.
ben.net: digging into dig traces. command:```dig @1.1.1.1 api.eu.example.com +trace +short``` results: sometimes empty, sometimes correct IP.
eve.infra: looks like CF edge resolvers are dropping responses for a subset of our delegated RRsets. Could be EDNS or TCP fallback issue. Cloudflare is showing elevated 5xx in their resolver pool for our zone.
carla.prod: customer impact: multiple EU customers reporting timeouts and some 502s from our edge proxies. Support queue rising. dave, please collect top 5 affected customers and their request IDs.
dave.support: collecting now — will post list in a sec.
carla.prod: also prepped status page draft. we should indicate partial outage to EU users and we are investigating.
ben.net: quick mitigation idea: shift geo-dns fallback to Route53-only for eu region so queries bypass Cloudflare's resolver pool for our delegation. This requires updating our authoritative config in the geodns controller to remove cloudflare as preferred resolver for eu weight.
alice.sre: agree that reducing dependency on CF resolver pool could buy time. but need to confirm propagation risk and TTLs. our current TTLs are 60s for the A/ALIAS records.
eve.infra: i can push a weighted change to geodns in 2 mins and increase Route53 weight to 100 for eu. will also bump healthcheck frequency.
frank.oncall: frank taking lead for handoff. summary for next oncall: the issue is intermittent NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL from Cloudflare resolvers for our eu delegation causing client errors at edge. action taken: geodns toggled to prefer Route53 in eu, cache invalidation requested at the edge, notifying Cloudflare support.
incident-bot: Note: on-call handoff scheduled at +30m. new primary: frank.oncall.
dave.support: posting affected customer list: customer-a (req-ids: r123,r124), customer-b (r200), customer-c (r301,r302), customer-d (r450). all EU-based.
alice.sre: after toggling geodns weights we are seeing a drop in 5xx rate from eu endpoints from 30% -> 8% within one TTL window. latency slightly higher for some queries due to route changes.
carla.prod: draft status update ready: "Partial degradation for EU users affecting API requests; teams are routing DNS away from Cloudflare resolvers and investigating with CF. Partial mitigation in place." Should I post?
frank.oncall: post it. include that customers can retry and that we have a mitigation active.
cloudflare-support-bot: Support ticket #CF-92134 opened with Cloudflare NOC. Preliminary: "Seeing intermittent recursive resolver failures for zone example.com, investigating EDNS UDP fallback behaviour"
ben.net: logs show some EDNS truncation and TCP fallback failures. sample tcpdump snippet:```17:04:22.123456 IP 1.1.1.1.53 > 10.0.0.5.54817: DNS 0x1a2b Standard query 0x1a2b A api.eu.example.com. + tc 0; flags qr aa; UDP truncated? fallback to TCP fails with RST from 1.1.1.1 in some flows.```
eve.infra: i'm going to open a temporary ACL rule to bypass problematic CF resolvers for our egress and force queries to route53 NS via our recursive forwarders. rolling in 30s.
alice.sre: please also purge edge caches for api.eu.* for 1 minute so we avoid stale errors while the DNS paths converge. command to purge CDN:```curl -X POST "https://api.cdn.example/v1/purge" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CDN_TOKEN" -d '{"prefix":"/api/"}'```
frank.oncall: monitor: dashboards show errors down but still some spikes. we should keep incident active until stable for 60m.
dave.support: PRs from customers indicating partial recovery, but one large customer still seeing failures. collecting traces.
carla.prod: liaising with account team for that large customer, providing mitigation steps (TTL flush, local DNS cache clear).
ben.net: Cloudflare support says they rolled a hotfix in their resolver pool for impacted nodes; they recommend we keep Route53 weight in eu for 1 hour to ensure stability, then revert if OK.
alice.sre: recommend we also enable TCP-only queries for our internal resolvers toward cloudflare temporarily — reduces UDP truncation impact. will push config.
eve.infra: done. queued change: forwarders set to prefer TCP for CF resolvers. returning to monitor.
frank.oncall: timeline for postmortem: start doc in #postmortems after incident declared resolved. owners: ben (root cause), alice (mitigation and telemetry), carla (customer comms).
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation in place (geodns -> Route53 for EU, forwarders prefer TCP). Next update in 15 minutes or on status change.
alice.sre: last check: 5xxs down to baseline (<=1%) for 20m. happy to close after 60m stable.
frank.oncall: closing loop: if we remain stable for 60m we'll post resolution and run RCA. handing off to frank for post-incident coordination.
carla.prod: posting final update to status page in 5.
frank.oncall: thanks all. good job. remember to include CF ticket id in postmortem notes.
cloudflare-support-bot: CF ticket #CF-92134 updated: "Root cause: partial recursive resolver TCP fallback regression affecting specific EDNS sizes; hotfix deployed and rollback of regressed code path performed."
frank.oncall: noted. starting RCA doc.
